title: Vocabulary: describing trends and comparisons for Writing Task 1
status: Owner approved v1.1.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Learners can read the axes of a line graph and a bar chart.
Pitched at learners aiming for Band 6.5-7.5 whose Task 1 answers are repetitive or describe the data inaccurately.

objectives.text: Choose trend language whose strength matches the data (plummet, level off, a marginal rise) and use it with accurate grammar.
Compare figures accurately with proportions, multiples and approximations (almost twice as much, just under a quarter, overtake).
Write an overview that identifies the main trends without numbers.

levels.foundation: Use the verb + adverb pattern only (rose sharply, fell slightly) and keep the word bank open while writing.
levels.core: Use at least one adjective + noun pattern (a sharp rise in ...) and two accurate comparisons in the paragraph.
levels.extension: Write one sentence that combines a trend and a comparison (for example: '..., overtaking coal between 2015 and 2020').
levels.high_band: Write the overview and two body paragraphs with no repeated trend word and every number supporting a key feature.

word_bank.example: Wind and solar power rose steadily.
The share of coal declined sharply after 2005.

word_bank.meaning: fall / rise very fast by a large amount
word_bank.example: Sales soared from 5% to 40% in two years.

word_bank.meaning: stop changing and stay at about the same level
word_bank.example: Gas remained stable at around a third.

word_bank.item: peak at / reach a peak of
a sharp / steady / slight + rise in / fall in
word_bank.meaning: noun pattern for trends (note the preposition 'in')
word_bank.example: There was a sharp fall in the share of coal.

word_bank.meaning: adverbs showing the speed or size of a change
be a particular proportion of a total
word_bank.example: Coal accounted for 58% of electricity in 2000.

word_bank.meaning: become larger than something that was larger before
comparison by multiplying (much for amounts, many for numbers)
word_bank.example: Teenagers spent three times as long on social media.

word_bank.meaning: introduce a different or opposite trend

word_bank.item: just over / just under / nearly / roughly
word_bank.meaning: give a number that is not exact
part of a total, usually a percentage
word_bank.example: The share of gas changed very little.

stages.title: Opening challenge: varied or accurate?
stages.student: Decide which sentence describes the change best before the reveal.
stages.say: A word must fit the size of the change. Variety comes second.
stages.check: Learners can say why 'soared' is wrong for gas.

stages.title: Word bank: strength and grammar
stages.student: Sort the word bank into 'up', 'down', 'no change' and 'compare', and rank the adverbs from smallest to largest change.
stages.teacher: Board a scale from 'marginally' to 'dramatically'. Drill the two patterns: verb + adverb, and adjective + noun + in.
stages.say: Two patterns: 'fell sharply' and 'a sharp fall in'.
stages.check: Learners transform three sentences between the two patterns.

stages.title: Which description is accurate?
stages.student: Choose the one accurate sentence each time. Check every number and every trend word against the graph.
stages.teacher: Eight minutes. During the reveal, ask learners to prove each wrong option wrong with a number.
stages.say: Check the numbers before you trust the words.
stages.check: Learners disprove each distractor with a figure from the graph.

stages.title: Comparisons on a bar chart
stages.student: Choose the accurate comparison each time.
stages.teacher: Six minutes. Focus on multiples (twice, three times) and on 'overtake'.
stages.say: Do the arithmetic: 18 is three times 6, not twice.
stages.check: Learners explain each multiple with the figures.

stages.title: Plan the paragraph
stages.student: Choose the three key features and the words you will use for each.
stages.teacher: Check plans quickly: the overview must contain no numbers.
stages.say: Plan the features first, then choose the words.
stages.check: Every learner has three features noted.

stages.title: Write independently
stages.student: Write the overview and one body paragraph.
stages.teacher: Twelve minutes, no model visible. Note who uses both trend patterns.
stages.say: Every number you include should prove a key feature.

stages.title: Compare with the model
stages.student: Underline the trend and comparison language in the model; then correct one inaccurate word in your own paragraph.
stages.teacher: Ask: which word in the model is strongest, and do the numbers justify it?
stages.say: The model is illustrative, not a target band.
stages.check: Each learner corrects one word or number.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the homework.
stages.say: In every Task 1 answer, check one comparison with arithmetic before you finish.
stages.check: Every learner writes one accurate comparison from memory.

blocks.title: Varied or accurate?
blocks.mode: Opening challenge; learners decide before the reveal
blocks.instructions: In one country, the share of electricity generated from gas rose from 30% to 32% between 2000 and 2020. Three learners described this change. Which sentence is best?

examples.label: Learner A
examples.text: The use of gas soared over the period.
examples.comment: Inaccurate: 'soared' means a very large, fast rise. Two percentage points is tiny.

examples.label: Learner B
examples.text: Gas remained relatively stable, rising only marginally from 30% to 32%.
examples.comment: Best: the words match the size of the change, and the numbers prove it.

examples.label: Learner C
examples.comment: Inaccurate: the share barely changed; 'dramatically' exaggerates.

blocks.title: Which description is accurate?
blocks.instructions: Look at the graph. Choose the sentence, A, B, C or D, that describes the data accurately. The other sentences are grammatical but contain an error of fact, strength or grammar.

figure.title: Electricity generated from three sources, one country, 2000-2020
figure.alt: Line graph of three sources of electricity from 2000 to 2020. Coal is almost unchanged at 58 and 57 per cent in 2000 and 2005, then falls to 49, 36 and 22. Gas stays between 30 and 33. Wind and solar rise from 2 to 4, 11, 24 and 41, overtaking coal between 2015 and 2020.

items.reason: A: coal barely changed before 2005, so 'steadily throughout' is wrong. C: 58 to 49 is not half. D: 36% in 2015 is over a third.
options: A  The share of coal fell steadily throughout the period.
B  The share of coal remained almost unchanged until 2005 and then fell sharply, to 22% in 2020.
C  The share of coal halved between 2000 and 2010.
D  Coal accounted for less than a quarter of electricity in 2015.

items.reason: B: 'soared' exaggerates a two-to-three point change. C: the line barely moves. D: in 2015 coal (36%) was still above gas (33%).
options: A  Gas rose marginally, peaking at 33% in 2010 and 2015.
B  Gas soared between 2000 and 2010.
C  Gas fluctuated wildly over the period.
D  Gas overtook coal in 2015.

items.reason: A: the increases were not equal. B: 11 to 41 is almost four times, not double. D: in 2010 wind and solar (11%) were far below gas (33%).
options: A  Wind and solar power grew by a similar amount every five years.
B  Wind and solar power doubled between 2010 and 2020.
C  The growth of wind and solar power accelerated, from 2% in 2000 to 41% in 2020.
D  Wind and solar power overtook gas in 2010.

items.prompt: When did wind and solar first produce more electricity than coal?
items.reason: The change happened between the 2015 and 2020 data points.
options: A  Wind and solar overtook coal between 2010 and 2015.
B  Wind and solar overtook coal between 2015 and 2020.
C  Wind and solar overtook coal before 2010.
D  Wind and solar never overtook coal.

items.reason: B would need 66%; C and D contradict the figures.
options: A  In 2020, wind and solar produced almost twice as much electricity as coal.
B  In 2020, wind and solar produced three times as much electricity as coal.
C  In 2020, wind and solar produced slightly less electricity than coal.
D  In 2020, wind and solar and coal produced the same amount of electricity.

items.evidence: a sharp fall IN the share of
items.reason: A uses the wrong preposition; C uses the -ing form as a noun after an adjective, which is not used here; D uses an adverb before a noun.
options: A  There was a sharp fall of the share of coal after 2005.
B  There was a sharp fall in the share of coal after 2005.
C  There was a sharp falling in the share of coal after 2005.
D  There was a sharply fall in the share of coal after 2005.

items.reason: 24% is just under a quarter (25%). B = about 34%; C = nearly 50%; D = exactly 20%.
options: A  In 2015, wind and solar accounted for just under a quarter of electricity.
B  In 2015, wind and solar accounted for just over a third of electricity.
C  In 2015, wind and solar accounted for nearly half of electricity.
D  In 2015, wind and solar accounted for exactly a fifth of electricity.

items.evidence: Main features: coal falls, wind/solar rises and becomes largest, gas stable
items.reason: A is false (coal fell); B is false (coal was largest at the start, wind and solar at the end); D is a detail with numbers, not an overview.
options: A  Overall, all three sources of electricity increased over the period.
B  Overall, gas was the largest source of electricity throughout the period.
C  Overall, wind and solar power replaced coal as the largest source of electricity, while the share of gas changed relatively little.
D  In 2000, coal accounted for 58% of electricity and gas for 30%.

blocks.title: Comparisons on a bar chart
blocks.instructions: Look at the bar chart. Choose the sentence, A, B, C or D, that describes the data accurately.

figure.title: Average weekly hours spent on four activities by teenagers, one city, 2010 and 2020
figure.alt: Bar chart comparing 2010 and 2020. Social media rises from 6 to 18 hours. Sport falls from 8 to 6. Reading falls from 5 to 3. Homework stays at 10.

items.evidence: 6 to 18 hours = three times as much
items.reason: A: 18 is three times 6, not double. B: the increase was 12 hours, not 18. D: 'slightly' understates a 12-hour rise.
options: A  Time spent on social media doubled.
B  Time spent on social media rose by 18 hours.
C  Time spent on social media tripled, from 6 to 18 hours a week.
D  Time spent on social media rose slightly.

items.reason: No change: it did not peak, fluctuate or fall.
options: A  Time spent on homework peaked in 2020.
B  Time spent on homework fluctuated around ten hours.
C  Time spent on homework fell marginally.
D  Time spent on homework remained unchanged at ten hours a week.

items.reason: A: 5 to 3 is not half. C: it fell to 3, not zero. D: reading (3) stayed below sport (6).
options: A  Time spent reading halved.
B  Time spent reading fell by two hours, the lowest figure for any activity in 2020.
C  Time spent reading plummeted to zero.
D  Reading overtook sport in 2020.

items.reason: B would need 30 hours; C and D contradict 18 and 10.
options: A  In 2020, teenagers spent nearly twice as long on social media as on homework.
B  In 2020, teenagers spent three times as long on social media as on homework.
C  In 2020, teenagers spent the same amount of time on social media and homework.
D  In 2020, teenagers spent half as long on social media as on homework.

items.evidence: 2010: homework 10 > social media 6; 2020: social media 18 > homework 10
items.reason: A: sport fell below homework in both years. B: reading stayed below sport. D: homework (10) stayed above sport (6).
options: A  Sport overtook homework.
B  Reading overtook sport.
C  Social media overtook homework as the most time-consuming activity.
D  Homework fell below sport.

items.evidence: Social media up; sport and reading down; homework unchanged
items.reason: A and B contradict the data; C is a detail with numbers, not an overview.
options: A  Overall, teenagers spent less time on every activity.
B  Overall, homework rose more than any other activity.
C  In 2010, teenagers spent six hours a week on social media.
D  Overall, social media was the only activity to grow, while time spent on sport and reading declined and homework stayed the same.

blocks.title: Overview and one body paragraph
blocks.mode: Independent classroom application after modelling; not a full Task 1 or Writing Screener
blocks.prompt: The graph shows the percentage of electricity generated from three sources in one country between 2000 and 2020. Write an overview and ONE body paragraph (about 120-150 words) describing the most important changes.

figure.title: Electricity generated from three sources, one country, 2000-2020
figure.alt: Line graph of three sources of electricity from 2000 to 2020. Coal is almost unchanged at 58 and 57 per cent in 2000 and 2005, then falls to 49, 36 and 22. Gas stays between 30 and 33. Wind and solar rise from 2 to 4, 11, 24 and 41, overtaking coal between 2015 and 2020.

blocks.conditions: 12 minutes, independent. No model visible. Record word-bank use.
blocks.support: Overview: Overall, ... while ... (no numbers). Body: start with the biggest change; use one verb + adverb pattern and one adjective + noun pattern; add one comparison.
blocks.high_band: No trend word may be repeated; every number must support a key feature.
blocks.model_label: Illustrative classroom model for discussion only. Not a certified band answer.
blocks.model:
Overall, electricity generation shifted from coal towards wind and solar power, which had become the largest source by the end of the period, while the share of gas remained relatively stable.

In 2000, coal accounted for 58% of the country's electricity, and this figure barely changed over the following five years. After 2005, however, there was a sharp fall in its share, which reached just 22% in 2020. Wind and solar power followed the opposite pattern: they produced a mere 2% at the start of the period, but their growth accelerated after 2010, and they overtook coal between 2015 and 2020, finishing at 41%, almost twice the figure for coal. Gas, by contrast, rose only marginally, from 30% to a peak of 33%, before levelling off at around a third.
checklist: Lexical Resource: Does each trend word match the size of the change?
Lexical Resource: Have you used both a verb + adverb and an adjective + noun pattern, with the right preposition?
Task Achievement: Does the overview give the main trends without numbers?
Accuracy: Is every comparison (twice, overtook, just under) correct when you check the arithmetic?

blocks.title: Homework: accurate and varied
blocks.mode: Homework; checked at the start of the next lesson
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-3: Rewrite each sentence with the noun pattern; write the missing word (ONE word). Questions 4-6: Check each sentence against the bar chart from the lesson. If it contains an error of fact or strength, rewrite it accurately; if it is already accurate, write 'accurate' and add the figures that prove it.

items.prompt: Prices rose slightly. → There was a ______ rise in prices.
items.reason: slightly → slight
Noun form; 'fluctuations' is also correct.

items.prompt: Exports increased considerably. → There was a ______ increase in exports.
items.reason: Adjective form.

items.prompt: Rewrite accurately: 'Time spent on sport plummeted between 2010 and 2020.'
items.answer: Time spent on sport fell slightly, from eight to six hours a week.
items.reason: 'Plummeted' exaggerates a two-hour fall; accept 'fell slightly', 'declined a little' or similar with correct figures.

items.prompt: Rewrite accurately: 'In 2010, teenagers spent twice as long on homework as on reading.'
items.answer: In 2010, teenagers spent twice as long on homework as on reading (ten hours compared with five).
items.reason: This sentence is already accurate (10 = 2 × 5). Accept 'accurate' with the figures ten and five; do not accept a changed comparison.

items.prompt: Rewrite accurately: 'Social media accounted for most of teenagers' time in 2010.'
items.answer: In 2010, homework took up the most time (ten hours a week), while social media accounted for six hours.
items.evidence: 2010: homework 10 is the largest; social media 6
items.reason: Social media was not the largest in 2010; accept any accurate correction.

exit_ticket: Two ways to say 'went down a lot', and one way to say 'changed very little':
One comparison I checked with arithmetic today:
The noun pattern, with its preposition:
homework: Complete the homework sheet, including the three accuracy corrections.
Find a chart in a newspaper or online. Write an overview (no numbers) and three accurate comparisons.

blocks.title: Fresh check: museum visitors
blocks.instructions: Look at the graph. Questions 1-4: choose the accurate sentence, A, B, C or D. Questions 5-6: complete each sentence with ONE word.

figure.title: Annual visitors to three museums, one city, 2014-2022 (thousands)
figure.alt: Line graph of three museums from 2014 to 2022. All three drop sharply in 2020. The science museum is highest in every year. The art gallery rises from 200 to 310, falls to 120 in 2020, then reaches 330 in 2022. The history museum stays between 140 and 155 apart from 60 in 2020.

items.prompt: The science museum and the art gallery in 2014
items.reason: A reverses the order; B would need 600; D would need equal figures.
options: A  In 2014, the art gallery attracted more visitors than the science museum.
B  In 2014, the science museum attracted three times as many visitors as the art gallery.
C  In 2014, the science museum attracted just over twice as many visitors as the art gallery.
D  In 2014, the two attracted the same number of visitors.

items.reason: A steady rise of over 50%; B and C contradict the data; D: the art gallery (310) remained below the science museum (430).
options: A  Between 2014 and 2018, the art gallery saw a steady rise in visitors.
B  Between 2014 and 2018, visitors to the art gallery fluctuated wildly.
C  Between 2014 and 2018, visitors to the art gallery fell slightly.
D  Between 2014 and 2018, the art gallery overtook the science museum.

items.reason: A: it fell in 2020; B: it was always lowest; C: it fell sharply in 2020 and then recovered, so 'steady fall' is wrong.
options: A  Visitors to the history museum rose every year.
B  The history museum was the most visited museum in 2022.
C  Visitors to the history museum fell steadily throughout the period.
D  Apart from a sharp drop in 2020, visitor numbers at the history museum remained relatively stable.

items.prompt: Which sentence would make the best overview of the museum data?
items.evidence: All fell in 2020 and recovered; science museum highest throughout
items.reason: A is false; C is a detail with numbers; D is false (the art gallery never overtook the science museum).
options: A  Overall, visitor numbers at all three museums rose steadily.
B  Overall, all three museums saw a sharp fall in 2020 followed by a recovery, and the science museum remained the most popular throughout.
C  In 2014, the history museum had 150,000 visitors.
D  Overall, the art gallery overtook the science museum as the most popular attraction.

items.prompt: In 2020, visitor numbers at all three museums ______ dramatically.
items.reason: Any verb meaning a large fall.

items.prompt: Visitors to the art gallery ______ at 330,000 in 2022, its highest figure on the graph.
items.reason: Highest point.
